parts.note: a round shape looks like the letter O
to fold something is to bend it over on itself

explanation.surface: Someone went mad many years ago.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Round the bend' reads as the slang for crazy, but it splits into O and FOLD, with 'the' only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an old-fashioned idiom for in former times, as in 'knights of old'.

definitions.meaning: coming loose from the clip that holds washing on a clothes line
bought already made rather than tailored to measure

explanation.surface: Something tumbling off a washing line is clothing bought from a shop rack.
explanation.definitionFit: Clothes bought straight from a rail in a shop, not made to measure, are said to be bought this way; the first reading is the pin that holds laundry.

parts.note: ahead by a single point, so 'singularly' is read as 'by exactly one'

explanation.definitionFit: A competitor ahead by one point, or having a small advantage over a rival, is said to be this.

clue.text: Derek, on river, has to remove parasites

parts.note: Del is a short form of Derek, as in Del Boy of the British sitcom Only Fools and Horses
the Ouse is a river in England (there are several)

explanation.surface: A man called Derek, living by a river, must rid himself of fleas.
explanation.walkthrough: The Ouse is the name of several English rivers, including the one through York.
explanation.definitionFit: To rid a person or animal of lice is a direct verb sense; the compound is literally 'take away lice'.

clue.text: Dust Kelvin, say, used in potentially explosive situation

parts.note: dust is fine powder
K is the symbol for the kelvin, the unit of temperature
'say' introduces an example, abbreviated e.g.

explanation.surface: A housework instruction to sprinkle dust and use Kelvin in a tense moment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Kelvin, say' looks like one example, but it gives two pieces: K for kelvin and EG for 'say'. 'used in' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A barrel of gunpowder is a literal bomb waiting to go off, used figuratively for any volatile, dangerous state of affairs.

parts.note: a heavy walking stick, made from a palm stem from a Malaysian island, has the joking name of a certain kind of lawyer, as it was used to settle disputes

explanation.walkthrough: A walking stick or cudgel made from palm wood was nicknamed after the Malaysian island it came from plus 'lawyer'; the clue asks for the place.
explanation.definitionFit: The island and state off the Malay peninsula gives its name to a cudgel known jokingly as its 'lawyer'.

clue.text: One engaged in a gripping sport

definitions.text: One engaged in a gripping sport

parts.words: One engaged in a gripping sport
parts.note: 'gripping' seems to mean thrilling, but the sport is one where competitors literally grab and hold each other

explanation.surface: A fan absorbed in a thrilling game.
explanation.definitionFit: A grappler in a sport of holds and throws spends the bout literally gripping an opponent.

indicators.note: the letter for river is placed in the middle of the word for leave out

parts.note: to except something is to leave it out or exclude it

explanation.surface: An instruction to drop the river from a piece of writing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leave out' looks like an instruction to drop something, but it is the word for exclude; 'in' then places the river letter inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A short extract taken from a longer text or piece of music is a passage from it.

definitions.meaning: full of fun and mischief
like a young cat that has not yet grown up into a full cat

explanation.surface: A frisky person who is still too young to be spiteful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'catty' seems to mean spiteful, but here it means 'like a grown cat': a young one is not there yet. 'but' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Coy, frolicsome behaviour is likened to that of a young cat, as in a kittenish smile.

clue.text: It is bogus to encompass enthusiasm

indicators.note: the words bogus and to surround the answer, which sits inside them across the gap

explanation.surface: Fake zeal is said to be all around.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' looks like part of 'to encompass' but is also where the run ends: 'bogus to' holds the letters. 'It is' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Hearty relish and zest in doing something is synonymous with enthusiasm.

parts.note: something given for nothing is free
a lance is a long weapon carried by a mounted knight

explanation.surface: A contractor is armed at no cost.
explanation.walkthrough: The word for a self-employed worker comes from medieval mercenaries, knights with a lance free for hire.
explanation.definitionFit: A worker who sells services to various clients instead of holding a permanent job is self-employed.

indicators.note: slashed is told to come first, so its synonym goes before the word is

parts.note: slashed means cut

explanation.surface: A skin being sliced before anything else.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first' puts CUT ahead of IS, the reverse of their order in the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the anatomical Latin term for the true skin, the dermis and epidermis together.

parts.note: hep is an old slang word for knowing or well informed, like hip
burn is the Scottish word for a stream

explanation.surface: A film star who is wise to a Scottish brook.
explanation.walkthrough: Audrey and Katharine are the two famous Hollywood actresses with this surname.
explanation.definitionFit: Audrey and Katharine, two Hollywood stars, share the surname, so the actress is an example of the definition.

indicators.note: to reconstruct is to rebuild in a new form, so the letters of Pedro and to are rebuilt

explanation.surface: A man called Pedro is told to rebuild a rocket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' looks like part of 'to reconstruct' but is fodder with 'Pedro'.
explanation.definitionFit: A self-propelled underwater weapon fired at ships is a kind of missile.

indicators.note: the word for proper is heard said aloud rather than spelt

parts.note: pukka, from Hindi, means proper or genuine in British slang

explanation.surface: A formal agreement that sounds correct.
explanation.walkthrough: PUKKA is British slang (from Hindi) for genuine or first-class; said in a non-rhotic accent it matches the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To pucker is to draw together into wrinkles, as lips do, which is a sense of contract.

clue.text: Old king accepted hubby could have found snug enclosed space

indicators.note: the name of the old king takes in the other letters, like a host accepting a guest

parts.note: Old King Cole is the merry old soul of the nursery rhyme

indicators.note: the letters of hubby could have been found in a different order, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A husband taken in by an old monarch might have discovered a cosy hideaway.
explanation.walkthrough: The old king is Old King Cole of the nursery rhyme. 'could have found' is an unusual anagram signal: the husband's letters could have been arranged otherwise.
explanation.definitionFit: A small cosy cupboard or nook, just big enough to sit or store things in, is a snug enclosed space.

indicators.note: about here means moved around, so the letters of ruin and note are mixed together

explanation.surface: Destroy a musical note concerning a tiny particle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' seems to mean concerning, but it shuffles RUIN and NOTE.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiny neutral particle with almost no mass that rarely interacts with matter is one type of subatomic particle.

clue.text: Although not a member of the cast is in touch

definitions.text: not a member of the cast
definitions.meaning: not appearing in the stage production
with the ball over the sideline, as in rugby or football

explanation.surface: An actor left out of the production is still keeping in contact.
explanation.walkthrough: In rugby and football 'touch' is the area beyond the sidelines, so a ball there is not live. 'Although' and 'is' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone outside the drama is not in it; a ball over the sideline is no longer live in the game.

clue.text: Where baked beans are it is agreed

definitions.meaning: inside a tin, the way beans are sold
finished and settled, as a completed film is

explanation.surface: Beans in a tin, and a deal is done.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It is' is a link. The film-industry phrase for a completed shoot is used for any matter wrapped up and settled.
explanation.definitionFit: Beans are sold sealed in a tin; a deal finished and settled is described with the same phrase as finished film footage.

clue.text: Follow being one turn in arrears

definitions.meaning: come after, trail someone
a go is a turn, so being a go back in the game

explanation.surface: Trailing someone while lagging a turn in a board game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one turn' is 'a go', so 'one turn in arrears' is literally a go behind.
explanation.definitionFit: To trail or pass after someone is to follow; read literally it is also a game's turn in arrears.

indicators.note: off means wrong or not right, so the letters of the rain are disordered

explanation.surface: Something worn on the head to stop getting wet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' looks like part of 'keeping the rain off', but it signals that THE RAIN is rearranged; 'keeping' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A fine mesh worn over the hair to hold it in place is a kind of covering for the head.

definitions.meaning: unfashionable, no longer new
an aged piece of millinery

explanation.definitionFit: Stale, overfamiliar ideas are called this idiom; literally the words also describe an aged bonnet or cap.

clue.text: Cultivated most of seedling for oil

indicators.note: cultivated land is turned over, so the letters are worked into a new order
most of the word seedling is used, dropping its final letter

explanation.surface: A gardener grew most young plants to produce oil.
explanation.walkthrough: 'most of' drops the last letter of SEEDLING, leaving SEEDLIN, and 'Cultivated' rearranges those letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Flax seed, pressed for the oil used on cricket bats and in paints, gives its name to that oil.

clue.text: Husband leaves port for leafy glade

indicators.note: husband departs from the word, so its letter is removed

parts.note: a harbour is a port

explanation.surface: A man departs from a harbour town for a shady wood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaves' seems to belong to the glade but signals that H (husband) is taken out of HARBOUR. 'for' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A shady garden retreat formed by trees or climbing plants is a leafy bower, close to a glade.

definitions.meaning: aim for great success
travelling far above the ground by air

explanation.surface: Aspiring to great things on a flight.
explanation.definitionFit: Aiming for great success is an idiom of soaring upward; literally it also describes a plane passenger far above the ground.

definitions.meaning: pay close attention, as a verb
the centre of interest or activity

explanation.surface: Fix your attention on the middle.
explanation.definitionFit: To direct one's attention is the verb sense; the hub or centre of activity is the noun sense.

clue.text: Hang up at end of engagement?

definitions.meaning: end a phone call
when a betrothal is broken, the betrothal band comes off

explanation.surface: Putting down the telephone when a betrothal is over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'engagement' reads as a phone line being engaged, but it is a betrothal whose ring comes off. 'at' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Ending a telephone call is an old British phrase for hanging up; literally it also pictures a betrothal band being removed.

clue.text: Ring fellow before one, one from middle east

parts.note: a ring is round like the letter O
a fellow is a man
the Roman numeral for one is I

explanation.surface: Calling a man before someone from the Gulf.
explanation.walkthrough: 'before' is a link putting MAN ahead of I, as it is in the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Belonging to the sultanate on the Arabian peninsula means coming from the Middle East.

parts.note: a quarter-pounder sounds like a burger, but here it is a coin worth a quarter of a pound sterling

explanation.surface: A fast-food burger fondly remembered.
explanation.walkthrough: This was an old British coin worth five shillings, which was a quarter of a pound before decimal money in 1971.
explanation.definitionFit: The old British five-shilling coin was worth a quarter of a pound sterling, so it was literally a quarter-pound piece.

clue.text: Visit next door, almost a disaster

definitions.meaning: a social visit made nearby
a narrow escape

explanation.surface: Popping round to the neighbours nearly ends in catastrophe.
explanation.definitionFit: A narrow escape is called this idiom; literally it is also a social visit made nearby.

definitions.meaning: an illicit payment offered as an inducement
a substance that adds sweetness

explanation.definitionFit: A payment that makes a deal more attractive is figuratively one; sugar or an artificial substitute is literally one.

clue.text: Bloomer is seen during time sun is above horizon

indicators.note: the word is appears inside, during the period of daylight

parts.note: the day is the time when the sun is up

explanation.surface: A flower seen in daylight hours.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bloomer' looks like a blunder or a loaf, but it is a flower: a thing that blooms.
explanation.definitionFit: A common white-petalled flower is a bloomer, since bloomers are plants that bloom.
